committed: Before any prototype existed: the seam's contract, the harness configuration, every bound, the decision function and the slices were committed in this file and in TIDAL_TORQUE_GATE.md ahead of the spike branch spike/tidal-torque-gate. The spike is never merged; production code is built afterwards, within the verdict only.

seam.where: js/engine/forces.js computeAccelerations, after the gravity sum and the MOND step, as a registered list of tidal pairs; every scheme (symplectic Euler, Velocity Verlet, RK4) reaches it, because every stage's acceleration comes from that function. Nothing else in the engine changes. A step with no registered pair executes one length test.
seam.law: a dissipative acceleration along the azimuthal unit vector of the pair's separation, equal and opposite on the two bodies in momentum (the force F = mu a_t on the moon, -F on the planet), with a relative magnitude a_t(r) = s lambda eps0 [G (M + m) / a0^2] (a0 / r)^7 and s = sgn(omega - n_inst); eps0 = (3/2) (k2/Q) (m/M) (R/a0)^5 is the kernel's constant-Q ratio of the tidal to the central acceleration at the starting separation a0 and lambda a stated rate multiplier that makes the secular change visible in a short run (the physical ratio is about 6e-13 for the Earth and the Moon)
seam.spin: the planet's spin omega is a side variable of the seam (the engine's bodies have none); it fixes the sign and carries the angular-momentum account: I domega/dt = -(r x F)_z on the moon, I = alpha M R^2
seam.conserved: linear momentum of the pair exactly (equal and opposite); the sum L_orbit + I omega to the quadrature of the torque; the total energy E_orbit + I omega^2 / 2 is NOT conserved: it falls by the dissipation D = integral of N (omega - Omega) dt >= 0 while omega > Omega, and the seam may never raise it
seam.notModelled: the conservative radial part of the tide (apsidal precession), eccentricity tides, spin-orbit resonances, the planet's finite size in the gravity, a variable Q; the law is stated for near-circular orbits with the spin ahead of the orbit

harness.units: the engine's own: G read from physicsSettings.gravitational_constant as the engine holds it; M = 1000, m = 10 (mass units), a0 = 100 (length units), a circular start about the centre of mass; R and k2/Q enter only through eps0
harness.omega: 1.5 n0 (spin ahead of the orbit); alpha 0.33
harness.reference: the same relative-orbit equations of motion integrated by scipy.integrate.solve_ivp (DOP853, rtol 1e-13, atol 1e-15) in the independent oracle venv; the semi-major axis a(T) at T = 20 initial periods from the vis-viva relation of the relative state; the kernel's closed form a(t)^(13/2) = a0^(13/2) + (13/2) s lambda C t is the second reference
harness.measure: err(N) = |a_N(T) - a_ref(T)| / a0 at the end of the run, from the engine's own bodies; the slope is the least-squares fit of log err against log dt over the three step sizes

G1.off.identity.what: with no pair registered, computeAccelerations returns bit-identical arrays and a seeded multi-step run of three scenarios (a binary, the Solar System at three bodies, a ring of twelve) is bit-identical to base; the world golden and the seeded-step equivalence tests pass unchanged

G2.zero.strength.what: a pair registered with lambda = 0 gives a trajectory bit-identical to the pair absent, under all three schemes

G3.closed.form.what: the change in the semi-major axis over the run, from the engine's bodies at the finest step, against the kernel's closed form

bounds.unit: relative to the closed form's change in a

G4.order.what: the measured slope of the error against the oracle's a(T)

G5.momentum.what: total linear momentum of the pair after the run, relative to m times the orbital speed, in the centre-of-mass frame the run starts in

G6.budget.what: the account: |DeltaL_orbit - integral of the torque| and |DeltaE_orbit - integral of F.v| over the run, each relative to the change itself, at the finest step, the integrals by the trapezoid rule on the step-end states

G7.dissipation.what: the total energy (orbit plus I omega^2 / 2, with omega from the angular-momentum account) never rises between consecutive samples during the run while omega > n, and its fall over the run is within 1 percent of the closed-form dissipation of the kernel

G8.overhead.what: the cost of the seam with an empty registry: the minimum over 7 interleaved repeats of 2e4 calls to computeAccelerations at 50 bodies, head against base, in one process

decision.A: G1 and G2 pass and G3 to G8 pass for all three schemes: the tidally evolving binary scenario ships with its proofs as tests
decision.B: G1 and G2 pass and at least one of G3 to G8 fails: a precomputed trajectory from the kernel is displayed, no force in the engine; the seam is not merged
decision.C: G1 or G2 fails (the seam cannot be made inert): no scenario; the kernel's plots stand
decision.rule: the first match from the top; a bound that proves unmeasurable fails the leg that holds it; only Carl resets a bound; a failed leg is reported and left failing, never moved, restated or widened

A: the seam in js/engine/forces.js behind a registered list
one built-in scenario, a tidally evolving binary, declared through the geometry table with its pair registered by the scenario's own rule
the proofs of G1 to G7 as tests in the suite
B: the kernel's evolveCircular trajectory sampled into a table and displayed as a plot and as a prescribed body pair (model_owned), no engine force
